solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Retire with some wine?

definitions.meaning: to retire for the night is to go to bed
playfully read as striking a bottle of sack, an old name for a dry sherry-like wine

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to bed taking a glass of something along.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is an old word for white wine imported from Spain, as in Falstaff's sack; the question mark flags the punning second reading of hitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for going to bed is a slangy way of saying one retires for the night.

clue.text: Overacting, his antics maybe miff you initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A ham actor's showy antics could irritate you.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a showy actor, so performance in that style is described by the related adjective.

clue.text: They brought gifts, new items, here, for exchange

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Presents are being returned: new items, brought here to swap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the Nativity story carried gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Furious about onlooker's first jeer of derision

indicators.note: about means the word for furious goes round the other letter

parts.note: furious means hot under the collar, hot

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of onlooker's

explanation.surface: An angry spectator jeers at a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes O from onlooker's, and 'about' puts HOT around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisive shout or laugh is a scornful cry, as in hooting with contempt.

clue.text: Giving extra flavour, special, with sugary coating

parts.note: a cake with sugary coating is iced

explanation.surface: A description of a special cake, extra tasty and frosted.
explanation.definitionFit: Food seasoned with pungent additions has had its flavour boosted.

clue.text: Extremely easy insult about attempts to hit coconut?

indicators.note: about means the snub word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or insult them
at a fairground coconut shy you throw balls; each throw is a shy

explanation.surface: A fairground scene where someone mocks the throws at the coconuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where balls are thrown to knock coconuts off stands. 'about' wraps the snub word around the throws.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushy is British slang for comfortable or undemanding; the superlative means most effortless.

clue.text: Crushed teen crime via series of films?

indicators.note: crushed means the letters of the three words are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A film series about youth crime, crushing a teenage delinquent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crushed' rearranges TEEN CRIME VIA. The definition is loose, hence the question mark: the answer is a realist documentary style of film-making, so a body of films in that style.
explanation.definitionFit: This French term names a naturalistic documentary film style, covering a whole group of movies made that way.

clue.text: Source of stout courage?

definitions.meaning: stout, the dark beer, is poured from a glass container
nerve or guts, in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang having the bottle means having nerve; 'stout' hints at both beer and bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer comes out of a glass vessel, and the same word is British slang for daring or nerve.

clue.text: Fixing car, I'm no expert on radio!

indicators.note: fixing means repairing, so the letters of the three words are reworked

explanation.surface: A motorist admits to being no mechanic, only good with the car radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi, the Italian inventor, pioneered wireless telegraphy and shared a Nobel prize for it.

clue.text: Lose weight? Finish off attempt in Irish county

indicators.note: finish off means remove the final letter from the dieting word

parts.note: to lose weight is to slim

explanation.surface: A dieter in western Ireland is told to finish the attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' drops the last letter from SLIM, leaving SLI.
explanation.definitionFit: This county lies on the north-west coast of the Republic of Ireland, in Connacht.

clue.text: Frenchman in safety vest

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words safety vest

explanation.surface: A Frenchman wearing a high-visibility safety vest.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common male given name in France, as with Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Contrite writer I provided with shelter

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: An author, sorry for something, is given somewhere to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone remorseful and sorry for wrongdoing feels the repentance this word describes.

clue.text: Silently forward: hint to European

parts.note: on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: Instructions to quietly pass a suggestion along to a European.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on the balls of the feet is how one moves without a sound.

clue.text: Descendant touring Channel Islands finding another one

definitions.note: another descendant, following the first word of the clue

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for a male child goes round the islands' abbreviation

explanation.surface: An heir travels round Jersey and Guernsey and comes across a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descendant' looks like the definition but builds the wordplay; 'another one' means another descendant. The Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey, lie off northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir or offshoot of a family line, so it is a further descendant.

clue.text: Partner in second Post Office application

parts.note: use means application, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: A spouse makes a second form application at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband or wife is one's partner in marriage.

clue.text: Meander in South with no clothes on cut short

indicators.note: cut short means drop the final letter from the word for unclothed

parts.note: with no clothes on means naked

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about in the south, stark naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the D from NAKED to give NAKE. 'Meander' is a verb here: to wind along like a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind or twist along a curving path is to move like a serpent.

clue.text: Not entirely relevant language

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for pertinent loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A remark that is only partly relevant to the conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter of GERMANE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the tongue spoken in Germany, Austria and much of Switzerland.

clue.text: Old northeastern ship is a joke

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel from the northeast is laughably bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A short quip delivered in a single sentence is a kind of gag.

clue.text: Soften, ultimately calm, English Lieutenant

indicators.note: ultimately means take only the final letter of calm

explanation.surface: An English officer, calm in the end, softens his attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow tender or less firm, as butter or a hard heart does, is to thaw.

clue.text: Star circle oddly ignored for moment

indicators.note: oddly ignored means the first, third, fifth letters and so on are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A star's orbit is briefly overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: From STARCIRCLE 'oddly ignored' keeps the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In an instant, as in 'in a jiffy', a very brief span of time.

clue.text: Hombre who stashes drink

indicators.note: stashes means the words Hombre who keep the letters tucked away inside them

explanation.surface: A man who hides away his liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A brew is a drink, from tea to home-made beer.

clue.text: Dropped off pelts needing treatment

indicators.note: needing treatment means the letters of pelts are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Animal skins were delivered to a tannery for processing.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is an idiom for falling asleep, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Trading centre in island provides drink

parts.note: a mart is a market, a centre of trade

explanation.surface: A market on an island serves cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth cocktail is a well-known alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Fail this time here after finally missing the cut

indicators.note: after means the time-and-place words come behind the end letters
finally means take the last letter of each of the three words missing, the and cut

explanation.surface: A sportsman fails to make the cut and is out of the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of 'missing the cut', and 'after' puts the time and place words behind them. 'the cut' looks like golf's cut, but is only there for its end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make no progress at all, which is to fail.
